question.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
question.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

Two source defects remain: q-105261 labels a row scaling as -1/2 although its displayed result requires +1/2; q-127043 has two mathematically correct radio choices, options 1 and 2, because opposite nonzero vectors are both parallel to the line. Its worked solution explicitly supports option 1. Independently, q-34218 has the unique decomposition b=2a1+4a2-2a3, giving product -16. In q-74558, every vector in the span has equal first and third coordinates, requiring k=0; coefficients (2,1) establish sufficiency. In q-74560, every vector in the span has third coordinate twice its first, requiring k=-24; coefficients (-2,-2) establish sufficiency. In q-105248, the first and third equations force s=1,t=-1, but these give second coordinate 6 rather than 5, so u is outside the plane. In q-105261, u=-b-2c gives st=2. The coefficients of t give parallel vectors in q-32785 and q-127043. For q-32817, the image shows P=(-1,3,2) and Q=(2,4,5); Q-P=(3,1,3), giving the selected parametric equations.
